claims.text: Adding SiC to ZrB2 will permit synthesis below 1700 °C.
Adding SiC to ZrB2 will improve oxidation resistance relative to single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Adding SiC to ZrB2 will improve structural integrity relative to single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Adding SiC to ZrB2 will improve resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion relative to single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The intervention produces a composite microstructure containing SiC particles distributed within a ZrB2 matrix.
SiC forms a protective SiO2 layer at high temperature.
The protective SiO2 layer enhances the oxidation resistance of the ZrB2-SiC composite.
SiC reinforces the ZrB2 matrix and thereby improves mechanical strength.
The chemical stability of SiC mitigates corrosion by liquid plating metals.
The proposed operating boundary includes oxidative exposure at temperatures up to 1500 °C.
The proposed operating boundary includes prolonged exposure to liquid plating-metal baths.
ZrB2-SiC specimens containing 10–30 vol% SiC can be evaluated after spark-plasma sintering or hot pressing below 1700 °C.
Failure to achieve synthesis below 1700 °C or improvement in any of oxidation resistance, structural integrity, or liquid-metal corrosion resistance would falsify the hypothesis.
